name: Maslam
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only segmental comparative studies of Kotoko (Tourneux 2003 consonant and vowel systems) and surveys; no grammar or prosodic description of Maslam itself.

sources.citation: Allison, Sean; Tourneux, Henry; Adam Mahamat (compil.). 2020. Bibliographie Kotoko - Kotoko Bibliography (version 09 07 2020). 22 pp. www.kotokoresources.net (= HAL halshs-02927626, no file on HAL).
sources.note: Bibliography only. Names the only Maslam-specific descriptions known: Gaou, Adam 1997 'Projet d'orthographe de la langue kotoko-maslam' (Projet Découvre la Langue, atelier de phonologie et de systèmes d'écriture, Ndjamena, SIL ms., 19 p.) and Gaou, Adam 1999 'Structures grammaticales de la langue kotoko-maslam' (atelier de grammaire, Ndjamena, SIL ms., 24 p.); also Bagley, R. Kelly & James Roberts 1991 'Kotoko Survey Report' (Yaoundé, SIL, 64 p.).

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2001 [publ. 2003]. Le système consonantique des langues dites « kotoko ». In E. Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics I (papers from the 1st BICCL, Leipzig 2001), 115-135. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL halshs-00349309 (author manuscript, 20 pp.). [= Glottolog ref 103766]
sources.note: Comparative consonant study of eight Kotoko varieties; gives a Maltam /maɬam/ consonant chart (preprint p. 2, p. 3) and tone-marked Maltam forms in the correspondence tables; remark 12 (preprint p. 18, p. 20): 'Il y a une fréquente inversion du schème tonal entre afadé et maltam.' Stress/accent is never mentioned.

sources.citation: kotokoresources.net (SIL-affiliated Kotoko resources site), pages 'Maltam' (fr/en) and 'Bibliographie'.
sources.note: Maltam page holds no resources: 'If you would like to develop resources for Maltam Kotoko (maslam), please contact us'.

sources.citation: LLACAN member page for Henry Tourneux (full publication list).
sources.note: Confirms Tourneux 2007 'L'inversion tonale en kotoko' (TCL IV, Köppe, pp. 121-127) exists (no file on HAL); no Maltam- or Sahu-specific title in the list.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2021. Le nom du souverain dans les parlers « kotoko » du Cameroun. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 7: 43-62. HAL halshs-03473327.
sources.note: Maltam forms of the word for 'ruler'; nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD).
sources.note: §8.4 (p. 216): of the four Kotoko North languages 'only Mpade (Mahamat 2005; Allison 2005b) has been the subject of linguistic studies'; §8.4.4 Maltam (p. 217): 'For Maltam, the only available data is a short wordlist (Allison n.d.). The consonant inventory is similar to Afade.. The surface vowels are the same as in Afade and Malgbe.' The reconstruction states 'No attempt has been made to reconstruct tone or stress.' No Maltam stress statement.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Maslam language'; Wikipedia (fr) 'Maslam' (cite Ethnologue 18, ALCAM 2012, Barreteau 1987, Frawley 2003).
sources.note: No phonology, tone or stress information; dialects Maslam (Maltam) and Sao/Sahu; 250 speakers in Cameroon (2004).

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2004 [HAL 2005]. Les marques personnelles en kotoko et en mafa/wandala (langues tchadiques de la branche centrale). In D. Ibriszimow & G. Segerer (eds), Systèmes de marques personnelles en Afrique (Afrique et Langage), 199-212. Louvain/Paris: Peeters. HAL halshs-00349287 (author manuscript, 31 pp.).
sources.note: Pronoun paradigms for Mal (maɬam = Maltam) and Sah (sahwə = Sahu) with tone marks (pp. 4-20); p. 5: 'Il y a inversion du schème tonal entre Afa / Gou et l'ensemble du groupe central ainsi que Mal / Mak et Yed.'; object-pronoun tables omit tone (p. 17). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page masl1241 (Maslam; dialects Nuclear Maslam nucl1689, Sao saoo1238; refs Tourneux 2003, Gravina 2014, Barreteau & Dieu 2000, Dimmendaal & Voeltz 2007, Campbell et al. 2022; 'meds' all a wordlist or less).
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all; nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2003 [2006]. Origine des consonnes doubles et de la nasale syllabique à l'initiale dans les parlers « kotoko » du Cameroun. Topics in Chadic Linguistics II, 133-140. Köln: Köppe. HAL halshs-00349264.
sources.note: Maltam mentioned once; discusses H/L tone on Goulfey forms; nothing on stress for any variety.

sources.citation: Gaou, Adam. 1999. Structures grammaticales de la langue kotoko-maslam. Projet Découvre la Langue, atelier de grammaire. Ndjamena: SIL, ms. 24 p.

sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Maslam listed in the Tourneux/Adam/Allison 2020 Kotoko Bibliography; a DYL ('Découvre ta langue') workshop write-up may carry a prosody note; not in Glottolog.
